subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students
title: The PCM Link That Needed 64 kbps, Not 32
featured_title: THE PCM LINK THAT NEEDED 64 KBPS, NOT 32

presentation.challenge: The voice channel bandwidth was 4 kHz. The data link was sized at 32 kbps and immediately overflowed.

practice.primary_question: How do sampling rate and bits per sample determine the minimum PCM bit rate?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Multiplying analog bandwidth by bits per sample while forgetting that the sampling rate must be at least twice the signal bandwidth.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 4 kHz analog signal encoded with 8 bits per sample requires only 4,000×8=32 kbps.
case_dna.why_plausible: The analog bandwidth is stated directly, so it is easy to treat bandwidth as if it were already the sampling rate.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Ideal Nyquist sampling requires fs≥2B=8 kSa/s. At 8 bits/sample, the raw PCM bit rate is 8,000×8=64 kbps.
case_dna.corrected_model: For ideal baseband PCM, first choose fs≥2B, then compute Rb=fs×n bits/sample. Framing or coding overhead, if present, is additional.

problem_statement: A voice signal is band-limited to 4 kHz and encoded using ideal PCM with 8 bits per sample. A link budget allocates 32 kbps by multiplying 4 kHz by 8 bits. The encoder produces twice that data rate. Diagnose the missing sampling factor, calculate the minimum raw PCM bit rate, and determine whether a 50 kbps channel can carry the stream without compression.
fixed_constraints: Ideal Nyquist minimum sampling is used

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The 32 kbps channel overflowed as soon as PCM started.
gates.prompt: Which rate was confused with analog bandwidth?

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Choose the correct PCM rate model

options.label: Use fs≥2B, then Rb=fs×bits/sample
options.reason: The analog bandwidth determines the minimum sampling rate through Nyquist.

options.label: Use Rb=B×bits/sample directly
options.reason: That treats analog bandwidth as sampling rate and misses the factor of two.

options.label: Use Rb=fs/(bits/sample)
options.reason: Each sample contributes multiple bits, so the rates multiply.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the raw PCM bit rate
gates.prompt: At the ideal Nyquist rate for a 4 kHz signal and 8 bits/sample, what raw bit rate (kbps) is required?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Read the encoder output
gates.result: The raw PCM output is 64 kbps.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the PCM rate
gates.prompt: Use fs=2B=8 kSa/s and Rb=fs×8 bits/sample. Enter Rb in kbps.
gates.hint: Find the sampling rate before multiplying by bits per sample.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Sampling and quantization both set the data rate

cards.text: A 4 kHz band-limited signal needs at least 8 kSa/s in the ideal Nyquist case.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the link budget
report: C1. The voice signal bandwidth is 4 kHz.
C2. Each PCM sample uses 8 bits.
C3. Therefore the required bit rate is 4,000×8=32 kbps.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It uses analog bandwidth as the sampling rate.

evidence_choices.label: fs=2×4 kHz=8 kSa/s and Rb=8 kSa/s×8=64 kbps
evidence_choices.reason: This follows the ideal sampling requirement and PCM bit-rate relation.

correction.template: The minimum raw PCM rate is {rate} kbps before any framing or coding overhead.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Choose a channel that can carry the raw stream

options.label: Use a channel capacity of at least 64 kbps before overhead margin
options.reason: The raw stream alone is 64 kbps.

options.label: Use the 50 kbps channel because it exceeds the 4 kHz analog bandwidth
options.reason: The relevant digital stream is 64 kbps.

options.label: Keep 32 kbps because each sample is only 8 bits

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the PCM-rate rule
gates.prompt: A 3 kHz signal is sampled at 8 kSa/s with 10 bits/sample. What raw PCM bit rate results?

options.label: 30 kbps
options.reason: That multiplies bandwidth by bits instead of using the stated sample rate.

gates.explanation: PCM bit rate equals samples per second times bits per sample.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the PCM capacity check
gates.confirmation: I confirm that PCM bit rate is based on sampling rate, not directly on analog bandwidth.

items.label: What failed
items.value: A 32 kbps link was allocated for a 64 kbps raw PCM stream.

items.value: Analog bandwidth was treated as sampling rate.

items.value: Apply Nyquist first, then multiply sampling rate by bits per sample.

seo.seo_title: PCM Bit Rate: Why a 4 kHz Signal Needs 64 kbps | FE E-036
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Case E-036: a 4 kHz signal encoded at 8 bits/sample needs 64 kbps at the Nyquist sampling rate, not 32 kbps.
seo.excerpt: Analog bandwidth is not the same as sampling rate. A 4 kHz voice signal can produce a 64 kbps PCM stream.
seo.direct_answer: For ideal PCM, sample a band-limited signal at fs≥2B, then multiply by the number of bits per sample. For B=4 kHz and 8 bits/sample, fs=8 kSa/s and the raw bit rate is 64 kbps.

faqs.q: What is the PCM bit rate for 4 kHz bandwidth and 8 bits per sample at Nyquist sampling?
Is analog bandwidth the same as PCM sampling rate?
faqs.a: No. Ideal Nyquist sampling requires at least twice the highest signal frequency or baseband bandwidth for the stated case.
